extraction_scope: Worker-6 adjudicated mechanism evidence from reopened XML sections, Figure 2/3/5 captions/images, and methods text; no unsupported figure-only exact values were invented.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: These CHR-derived peptides interact with HIV-1 gp41 NHR peptide N46 and form six-helix-bundle-like complexes by CD spectroscopy.
mechanism_claims.limitations: CD supports 6-HB-like complex formation; it does not by itself explain the superior YIK-C16 antiviral potency.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: All three peptides inhibit HIV-1-mediated cell-cell fusion, with YIK-C16 showing lower IC50 in the local Figure 3a source.
mechanism_claims.limitations: Fusion assay supports fusion-inhibition mechanism but not direct antimicrobial membrane disruption.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Target-cell/virus wash experiments support membrane attachment/enrichment as the source-reviewed explanation for YIK-C16 improved anti-HIV activity.
mechanism_claims.limitations: Evidence supports membrane anchoring/enrichment in the HIV entry assay context; it is not generalized as broad membrane permeabilization.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Figure 5 and the cytotoxicity section support no detected in vitro cytotoxicity to MT-2 or M7 cells at the highest tested concentration, bounding toxicity rather than proving absence under all conditions.
mechanism_claims.limitations: Cell viability bars are graphical; exact per-concentration viability percentages were not fabricated.
